newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms ratings for Ontario, Ontario Hydro.
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms ratings for Ontario, Ontario Hydro.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Thursday it confirmed its debt ratings for the Canadian province of Ontario and Ontario Hydro, the government-owned power utility.
The rating agency said it confirmed the province's long- term debt at A (high) and short-term obligations at R-1 (middle).
Ontario Hydro's long-term debt was confirmed at A (high) and its short-term obligations at R-1 (middle).
All ratings carry stable trends, DBRS said in a statement.

"The ratings reflect the province's strong commitment to achieving its deficit targets, reduction of program spending to a more sustainable level, and a well diversified economy that is beginning to grow at a stronger pace," the rating agency said.

DBRS said the province is on track to eliminate its budget deficit by 2000-01. Last month, Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves forecast a C$6.6 billion deficit in fiscal 1997/98, down from C$7.5 billion in fiscal 1996/97.
The rating agency, however, expressed concern about government tax cuts.

"Implementation of the 30 percent personal income tax rate reduction increases the province's reliance on continuing strong economic growth to reach its balanced budget objective," the statement said.
Other challenges include lower federal transfer payments, a high deficit to GDP ratio, the restructuring of public services and financing requirements remain high.
The potential de-regulation of the electric utility industry coupled with Ontario Hydro's large debt load could present a further challenge to the province.
